html:
The Miskito Kingdom was a state of the Miskito people on the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and Honduras, allied with Britain from the 1600s until Nicaragua took it over in 1894. The coast was known as the Mosquito Coast.

The Miskito, a people of Indigenous and African descent, traded with English buccaneers and settlers for guns, and raided Spanish towns. England crowned their kings, and the coast stayed outside Spanish rule. Bluefields became its chief town, with English-speaking Creoles and later Moravian missions.

Britain gave up its protectorate in 1860, leaving a self-governing reserve. In 1894 President José Santos Zelaya sent troops and annexed it. The coast still has its own languages, faiths and autonomy, separate in many ways from the Spanish-speaking west of Nicaragua, the land the Mosquito Coast page describes.
